title: 2005 AMC 12B Problem 22
statement: A sequence of complex numbers \(z_0,\) \(z_1,\) \(z_2,\) \(\ldots\) is defined by the rule \[ z_{n+1} = \dfrac{i z_n}{\overline{z_n}}, \] where \(\overline{z_n}\) is the complex conjugate of \(z_n\) and \(i^2 = -1.\) Suppose that \(|z_0| = 1\) and \(z_{2005} = 1.\) How many possible values are there for \(z_0?\)

solutions.text:
Because \(|z_0| = 1,\) every \(|z_n| = 1,\) so \(\overline{z_n} = \dfrac{1}{z_n}\) and \[ z_{n+1} = \dfrac{i z_n}{\overline{z_n}} = i z_n^2. \]

Iterating, \(z_1 = i z_0^2\) and \(z_2 = i(i z_0^2)^2 = -i z_0^4.\) Moreover, if \(z_n=-i z_0^{2^n},\) then \(z_{n+1}=i(-i)^2z_0^{2^{n+1}}=-i z_0^{2^{n+1}}.\) Thus \(z_n=-i z_0^{2^n}\) for every \(n\ge2.\)

The condition \(z_{2005} = 1\) is therefore \(z_0^{2^{2005}} = i.\) Every nonzero complex equation \(z_0^{N} = i\) has exactly \(N\) distinct solutions, all on the unit circle.

Here \(N = 2^{2005},\) so there are \(2^{2005}\) possible values for \(z_0.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Iterating gives \(z_n\) as a fixed constant times \(z_0^{2^n}\); count roots of the resulting equation
